data.name: Fidaar
data.gender_notes: Fidaar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who assists and supports, a supporter, a helper, a trustee, a believer, a protector. The name Fidaar carries the meaning “Supporter, Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Fidaar usually hope their child will grow to embody supporter, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for someone who is always there to support and help others in their spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Fidaar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supporter, Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fidaar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: فدار
in_arabic.meaning: فداء أو فدية، تقديم شيء قيّم كفداء أو عوض
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مشتق من الفداء، وهو تقديم شيء قيّم كفداء أو عوض. يدل على معنى التضحية والإيثار في سبيل الله أو النجاة من شيء ما. ورد في القرآن الكريم في سياقات متعددة، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَنْفَضُوا مِنَ الدُّنْيَا وَاسْتَقْبَلُوا الْآخِرَةَ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً' (الآية 57 من سورة آل عمران)، حيث يظهر مفهوم الفداء والتضحية في سبيل الله.

in_urdu.name: فدار
in_urdu.meaning: فدائی یا قربانی دینے والا، اللہ کی راہ میں کچھ قیمتی دینا
in_urdu.long_meaning: فدار نام کا مطلب ہے فدائی یا قربانی دینے والا۔ یہ نام عربی زبان کے الفاظ سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی راہ میں کچھ قیمتی دینا یا اپنی جان یا مال کی قربانی دینا۔ اسلامی تقالید میں اس کا بڑا روحانی اور مذہبی اہمیت ہے کیونکہ یہ دکھاتا ہے کہ کوئی شخص اللہ یا دینی مقاصد کے لئے کچھ بھی دینے کو تیار ہے۔ تاریخی طور پر، ایسے ناموں کا استعمال ان خصوصیات کو ظاہر کرنے کے لئے کیا جاتا تھا جو ایک مسلمان میں ہونی چاہئیں۔

in_hindi.name: फिदार
in_hindi.meaning: फिदाई या कुर्बानी देने वाला, अल्लाह की राह में कुछ कीमती देना
in_hindi.long_meaning: फिदार नाम का अर्थ है फिदाई या कुर्बानी देने वाला। यह नाम अरबी भाषा के शब्दों से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है अल्लाह की राह में कुछ कीमती देना या अपनी जान या माल की कुर्बानी देना। इस्लामी परंपरा में इसकी बड़ी आध्यात्मिक और धार्मिक महत्ता है क्योंकि यह दिखाता है कि कोई व्यक्ति अल्लाह या धार्मिक उद्देश्यों के लिए कुछ भी देने को तैयार है। ऐतिहासिक रूप से, ऐसे नामों का उपयोग उन विशेषताओं को प्रकट करने के लिए किया जाता था जो एक मुसलमान में होनी चाहिए।

in_pashto.name: فدار
in_pashto.meaning: فدائی یا قربانی ورکوونکی، د الله په لاره کې څه قیمتي ورکول
in_pashto.long_meaning: فدار نوم معنی دے فدائی یا قربانی ورکوونکی. دا نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې معنی یې دے د الله په لاره کې څه قیمتي ورکول یا خپله ژوند یا مال قرباني کول. په اسلامي دود کې دا لوی روحاني او مذهبي اهميت لري ځکه چې دا ښيي چې کوم څوک د الله یا مذهبي مقاصدو لپاره څه هم ورکولو ته چمتو دی. تاريخي پلوه، داسې نومونو کارول د هغو ځانګړتیاوو د ښودلو لپاره کیده چې په يوه مسلمان کې بايد موجوده وي.

in_english.name: Fidaar
in_english.meaning: One who sacrifices or gives something valuable
in_english.long_meaning: Fidaar is an Arabic name that signifies a person who sacrifices or gives something valuable, often in the way of Allah or for a noble cause. The term originates from the Arabic root 'F-D-Y,' which appears in the Quran, emphasizing the concept of sacrifice and redemption. Historically, such names were chosen to reflect desirable traits in a Muslim, such as selflessness and devotion. The name carries significant spiritual and cultural weight across Islamic traditions.

data.cultural_impact: In history, Fidaar was an influential figure in India known for his unwavering loyalty and acts of service. He was a Revenue Officer in the Maratha province, reputed for his fair governance and unwavering support to the weak and oppressed.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Fidaar signifies unwavering faith and devotion to God. It is the belief that a true believer, like Fidaar, shall always have the back of fellow believers, empathizing with their struggles, following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad and upholding justice and fairness in all circumstances.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Fidaar symbolizes selfless devotion and sacrifice in the path of Allah. The one who bears this name is believed to be steadfast and unwavering in their commitment to their faith. They embody the spirit of giving and are willing to put themselves in harm's way for the sake of Allah and His creation.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah The name Fidaar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Battle of Uhud: Fidaar ibn Al-Harith Al-Kindi was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). During the Battle of Uhud, he was martyred while defending the Muslim army against the invading Quraysh forces. His sacrifice was instrumental in the Muslims' eventual victory.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd's Kitab Al-Tabaqat Al-Kabir The name Fidaar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Fidaar ibn Al-Yasar Al-Khuzai: A prominent companion and one of the Ansar (helpers) of Muhammad (pbuh) in Medina. He was killed while defending Medina against an invading Jewish force led by the Banu Qaynuqa'. His sacrifice helped to ensure the safety of the Muslim community in Medina.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Fidaar' originates from the Islamic concept of 'waqf', where assets are donated for charitable purposes. In a modern context, Fidaar refers to a pledge or commitment made by an individual or a community towards a specific cause, often in the form of a microfinance loan or a crowdfunding campaign. This concept is gaining popularity in the fields of Islamic finance, social entrepreneurship, and crowdfunding, where it is used to fund various social, educational, and economic projects. Platforms such as MicroMajlis in Indonesia, MicroRise in Turkey, and Kiva globally, enable individuals to make Fidaar pledges and contribute towards projects that align with their values and beliefs. The trend towards Fidaar is also driven by the increasing importance of social impact in business and finance, as well as the growing awareness of the potential for collective action to create positive change.
